notes: The army and all equipment-and-pet loadouts are exactly the user's logged TH16 army, overriding the guide's usual most-common-source composition rule. This is the new fireball-warden family; four supplied extractions use super-minion-air and T7jZVhq_JU0 uses other.

Only the five supplied relevant extractions and matching transcripts were used. Quotes and verified_t values were checked against those transcripts. Citation timestamps are video offsets, not battle times; t: 0 represents the narrated start.

Support counts distinct videos describing an action or rule, not separate attacks within a video. Support for an action does not imply identical placement, quantity or timing in every supporting example; those differences are identified here and in variants.

pTmX2vmv4sc carries eight Rocket Balloons, six Super Minions, three Furnaces and two Druids. o6YZ54fqojc carries nine Rocket Balloons, five Super Minions, three Furnaces and one Druid. 12Z_sTAEOHw carries eleven Rocket Balloons, two Furnaces and Clan Castle Super Minions, with Royal Champion replacing Dragon Duke. 7rzBODLfnug carries twelve Rocket Balloons, five Super Minions and two Druids. T7jZVhq_JU0 does not state a complete composition. Their spell totals, reinforcements, equipment and pets also differ.

Unavailable Flame Flinger sections and payload releases, Royal Champion steps, Baby Dragon funnels, Super Wall Breakers, Yeti, Goblin, Valkyrie, extra Furnaces or Druids, Freeze, Poison, Rage and Revive actions are omitted. The compatible Log Launcher entry is retained. The logged Clan Castle Ice Golem and Super Yeti remain its payload, not additional free deployments.

Earthquake Boots wall opening, Magic Mirror clones, Stun Blaster stuns and Angry Jelly defense targeting are omitted. The King ability retains the sourced Spiky Ball damage component with Stick Horse equipped. Duke deployment and troop support remain usable with Rocket Backpack, Fire Heart and Diggy, without assuming the videos' pet targeting or stuns.

No fixed attack-relative delays or repeat cadence are supplied. Every after trigger therefore uses delay: 0. Waits for outside defenses to fall, the correct Fireball position, completed funneling and useful pre-Recall clearing have no exact vocabulary trigger; preceding preparation steps approximate them. No destruction percentage or numerical health threshold is invented.

edge:charge, edge:main and edge:funnel represent scouted roles, not fixed clock positions. edge:funnel approximates the safer recalled-Warden area and separate Duke flank. Rocket Balloon placement uses the charge edge nearest the narrated outside defense. group_inside: main approximates the later Duke section after the hero dive progresses.

The two Earthquake casts are separate steps. building:mono is the concrete surviving-core-defense anchor from 12Z_sTAEOHw, so this default targets a Monolith-containing Fireball cluster. Other examples target different clusters, including the Clan Castle area. The sources support two follow-up casts, not an invented schedule spending all five logged Earthquakes; three remain unassigned.

o6YZ54fqojc explicitly deploys Healers immediately after Fireball but does not state their deployment count; all uses the logged five. The other extractions do not establish initial Healer timing. The early two-Furnace timing follows T7jZVhq_JU0 and examples in 12Z_sTAEOHw. o6YZ54fqojc deploys them after Fireball, represented in the quick-Fireball variant; its later third Furnace is omitted.

Recall follows the opening Fireball and Healer deployment with no invented clearing delay. Some examples instead recall only when the Warden or Healers are threatened. Redeploy returns the captured group together; the sources do not establish that every Healer or pet is always recalled.

all means remaining logged troops, not a claim that the source states that deployment count. The early Rocket Balloon count of one follows explicit examples in 12Z_sTAEOHw and 7rzBODLfnug; T7jZVhq_JU0 describes an unspecified few. Remaining Rocket Balloons and Super Minions support the Duke. Additional early groups and a separate Super Minion funnel lack a reliable shared allocation.

Protection policies have no precise cadence. Individual spell steps represent one cast opportunity: one Totem for Warden protection and one for a surviving Monolith engagement with the Duke, within the two carried Totems. threat:charge approximates the unspecified Warden Totem placement; heavy_fire approximates the narrated danger. The Duke Totem has no surviving target if the Monolith was already destroyed.

Warden Invisibility uses defenders_near as the closest trigger for the specifically narrated defending King attack. This broader proxy cannot enforce the cited warning about redirecting damage onto Healers. Duke Invisibility uses heavy_fire for the dangerous entry. Neither protection policy is converted into an invented repeating interval.

The three-Invisibility variant uses the lower end of T7jZVhq_JU0's three-to-four recommendation and the three-cast Rage Tower example in 12Z_sTAEOHw. It spends all three logged Invisibility Spells and removes both defensive Invisibility steps. Exact redirection placements are unspoken; threat:charge approximates intervening defenses and cannot guarantee the intended target. The four-cast setup exceeds this army's inventory.

The Wall Breaker variant uses ordinary Wall Breakers from o6YZ54fqojc, not substituted Super Wall Breakers. Druid timing is approximated after Queen entry: o6YZ54fqojc pairs it with a Queen ability using a different loadout, while pTmX2vmv4sc recommends earlier support for the Action Figure giant. No Magic Mirror activation is copied.

The Giant Arrow variant retains pTmX2vmv4sc's opened-core shot with the logged equipment. Its cleared-approach prerequisite and exact firing line are not expressible in the listed vocabulary, so after Queen deployment with delay: 0 is an approximation. No shared Rocket Backpack activation timing is inferred from Stun Blaster or Revenge Deck actions.

Wizard, Balloon, remaining cleanup Archer and Minion deployments have no additional precise shared placement-and-timing policy encoded here. Wall Breaker, Headhunter and Druid deployments are provided as a variant. Unallocated troops and spells remain in the logged army. No manual Log Launcher release time is stated.

12Z_sTAEOHw and T7jZVhq_JU0 explicitly concern TH16; the other extractions do not state a numerical Town Hall level. 12Z_sTAEOHw describes TH16 attacks against TH18 bases under Legends modifiers and includes failed plans. These are source-described tactics, not real-game calibration results for the logged army.
